author: Christopher T
review_text: If you haven't been or heard of this place, well now you do.  It just fantastic foods, services and in the street of okey neighborhood in a RA store parking lot.  I knew about this place for awhile but unable to come during their opening since they open late in the day til night time plus in LA - it's 45mins drive for us.  Finally,we make it here after the whole yr waiting.  It was 30mins standing in line for us in a cold Saturday night (7pm) but can't complaints since everyone infront or behind us had been here ALOT (plus their other location about 5-10mins away) so it's that good and got us excited more, especially we just drove back from SF and stuck in freeway traffic for 3 blocks plus haven't ate since 11am, you we saved for this.  The guys and the lady are very friendly, warm, helpful and nice to us and everyone else too...we're new so they explained and shown us what needed.  We got 15 tacos of mixed (beef, pork, head, tongue) with pineapple and a burrito of 2 meats.  Man, I ate ALOT of tacos & burritos (street foods that is) but this place just got me to a new level  appreciation for the foods and the family members working there.  The meats are just tendered, well seasoned, well displayed and well put together right infront of you (no hidden - what you ask is what you see and what you will eat).  The portion of each is HUGE...each taco can make into 2-3 more tacos (pov that is).  For burrito, after they got you the meats (I added cheese into it,, it melted with the tortilla (burned abit which make it soo soo good) and they give it to you to add what ever you into it, sauce, veggies l, grilled onions and you have it back to them to wrap it tightly and wrapped it with the aluminum.  The prices are just unbeatable for sure (well I know $1/taco street taco truck but the quality definitely can't compete with this place).  The massive self serve side veggies & sauces are massive - they do have drinks too.  We ate and ate and finished them all for 3 people and we just die and went somewhere and came back.. and wished we could have more room for more tacos and we also want to get quesadilla but the line is still long and we can't move.  All we can think is we make it here, we did it, we ate and will work on the schedule to come back one more time before this yr ends...man, my stomach is making noises from writing this and looking at last night pics of the foods.  Wish they're open all day.

author: Zerlina Zeng
review_text: Best taco in the US. We had a really good taco in Mexico City 10 years ago and have been looking for the similar taste ever since. We found it here. The staff are extremely friendly as well

author: Karrie
review_text: Probably one of the best taco places in LA. We think about wanting to go every once in a while. $2/taco.

author: Jamisen Wrinkle
review_text:
Wow… just wow….
Never thought a food stand on the side of the road could make me feel this type of way. I discovered this place on TikTok while scrolling on the toilet. Immediately I knew I needed to try this. I approached the stand only to find a group of long lost family members smiling and making me feel welcome. For the first time I was a true “Hermano.” You could instantly tell these people were masters of their crafts. The only thing finer than their slices were the prices. I’m debating making this a daily routine to visit my newfound brothers and cousins. The service was impeccable and the food was making me salivate like a rabid dog. I ordered a top 2 burrito I’ve ever had in my life (and it isn’t 2). The smell and the taste is to die for. I will warn that they are closed on Mondays unfortunately.

author: G R A C E
review_text: Delicious street tacos and you can choose your own toppings!

author: Diego Galindo
review_text: Took one bite in the car and had to pull over to give them five stars. Absolutely the best tacos I have ever had and I grew up in Guadalajara. A MUST try in LA. 🤙🏽

author: Ariya Prongsirikul
review_text: Friendly staff and delicious taco nearby! The price is very affordable. If you are okay with street food, standing eating, very recommend!

author: flat rate
review_text: Everything about this tacos is amazing. Whoever didn’t try it. You have to run and you’re gonna need to stay in line. The people are amazing. The food is amazing. Only good things. I’m going there at least three times a week and it’s not expensive. Where are you? Gonna find a burrito for $10.

author: Yannah Melle
review_text: Great tacos- super tasty, good price, has every side/ addition you could want. there’s even music playing. Has an organized  ordering line and the chefs and staff were very friendly and attentive. So happy I ran into this walking to Vons. Has a few stools to sit on if you want to eat there. A table or two would be nice since gets pretty crowded but eating on the parking barrier on the side of the road w everyone still a vibe you know

author: William Davidson
review_text: There are plenty of amazing taco stands in LA. This is as good as it gets.

author: benjamin archibeque
review_text:
I feel extremely fortunate to be living in the street taco era here in west L.A. I myself am an Al Pastor lover & I actively seek for new places that offer it. I actually judge street taco vendors by the quality of their a
Al Pastor & if they rotate it on a pike. I feel like there are so many options out there & I have yet to try them all, but I can honestly say this place is in the top 5 for me all time. I've had Al Pastor in San Diego, east L.A., etc. For me, I prefer a taco vendor that doesn't cook all the meat in one grease pot. I know a lot of people like this, but I do not like when my meat is mixed with all other types of meat, including intestine, tongue, etc.. I like that they separate the meat, and I like it when the Carne Asada has a smoky barbecue kind of taste to it. This place offers my exact preferences and is a diamond in the rough. For all you taco connoisseurs I strongly recommend that you give this place a try. This place is getting more popular now, my days of eating here without a line are soon to be gone. Enjoy friends.

author: Kym Ikeda
review_text:
Authentic Street Tacos Done Right

Brothers Cousins Tacos nails the street taco experience—quick, flavorful, and satisfying. The meats are tender and well-seasoned, whether you go with asada, carnitas, or lengua. Each taco is made fresh to order, and the salsa station is always clean and well-stocked.

The casual setup makes it perfect for a quick bite during the day or a late-night taco run. Prices are fair, portions are generous, and you can customize your plate with extras like caramelized onions and potatoes.

Service is fast and efficient! You’ll have your food within minutes, and it’s fun to watch them prepare everything right in front of you.

If you're looking for no-frills, high-flavor tacos, this spot definitely delivers. I’ll be back for more!

author: Daniel Jeong
review_text: One of the best burritos in LA so def come here to try some. They give great portions of meat and their pastor marinade is incredible. I went to the one at Sawtelle but there are two locations

author: Baltazar Perez
review_text:
I love the tacos here because they are delicious!
And like everything good, after a great taco, an Elote or Esquite 🌽 that they sell on the side of the taco stand and they have fresh churros made right in front of you and fried plantains too. 😋 I recommend this place 100% ✅

author: BOBBYRACECAR
review_text: Solid tacos with a lot of options and choices, I would suggest getting the burrito over the tacos…felt like I was at a family cookout while waiting in line. Would not wait again in line for 1+ hr…

author: Jed Kwon
review_text:
Amazing. I've become so irritated because I've been trying to find a good taco place near LAX, finding slight differences and improvements at the different taco stands and I try this place and it blows away every other taco place I've been to in all categories. Taste, variety, presentation, customer interaction. Literally better than any place I tried, at a competative price too. It's infuriating that this place is so far away from where I work.

Only complaint is their guacamole salsa isn't as good but hardly anything worth mentioning.

author: Louis Mora
review_text: The Tacos and Quesadillas were on point definitely check them out if you’re in the area.

author: LegendaryEats
review_text:
Portions are bigger than anywhere else

People line up to get the best bang for their buck

Lots of meat choices
No tables it keeps cost down

Burritos are stuffed by you
It's your choice of condiments
Really love the pickled spicy onions with habanero

author: Matthew Howell
review_text: My absolute favorite place to get tacos in all of LA! Their quesadilla has always been a standout for me, especially with carne asada and extra meat. You can't go wrong with this place.

author: Daphne Williamson
review_text: Best al pastor in LA and they bump 90s hits. Almost makes you forget you’re eating off the trunk of your car in a rite aid parking lot.

author: Jacky Lam
review_text: Came here 3 years ago. The food was amazing. Back again today, a little disappointed on the overall taste of the food. The crispy pork Kra Pao was very dry, tough, and not crunchy. The pork leg was very dry and not as juicy as before. Still good, but not as good as before or in Thailand. Sorry to give this place 3/5, from 5/5.

author: Jeffrey A Brick
review_text:
June 12, 2025, 10:22 PM PDT
Nestled on Hollywood Blvd., Ruen Pair, a quarter-century beacon in Thai Town, welcomed me into its snug, buzzing dining room—a true community of spice-seekers.

Vegetable Egg Rolls arrived first: golden, crisp shells hiding cabbage, carrots, mushrooms, and glass noodles. With a dance of sweet‑sour sauce—vegetarian if you mind to check the fish sauce—it was a lively, light opener, priced at a modest $7–$9.

Then came Pad Kee Mao with Tofu (~$11–$13), the meal’s bold heart. Flat noodles, chewy and hearty, twirled with bell peppers, onions, garlic, chili, and fragrant Thai basil. Ordered “medium” spicy, it struck that ideal note—vivid, aromatic, and spirited without beating you down  ￼ ￼.

My drink, misnamed “Tom Yum Beer,” turned out to be a Thai iced tea with coconut milk (~$5). It cooled the tongue’s fire splendidly; whether it was truly inspired by Tom Yum or just happy accident, it paired just right.

Service was unassuming yet attentive—no hovering, but enough care to note my lack of egg and offer to omit it. The dinner tab came to about $36.50 before tax—a fair exchange for flavors this honest and vivid.

The dining room was a lively mix: Indian, Korean, white Angelenos—all tucked shoulder to shoulder, savoring the same healthy kick of spice. No frills, just authentic Thai done right.

If your palate calls for chewy noodles, crisp bites, and a dash of well‑tempered fire in the heart of Los Angeles, Ruen Pair stands ready. Even a modern Twain would tip his hat.

author: Osama Malik
review_text: This place has excellent Thai food. I visited with a group of three and there was a bit of a line but it moved quickly. I had some morning glory and pad see ew with shrimps. The morning glory was pretty tasty and a good appetizer. The pad see ew was a bit too spicy, which was my fault, since that’s what I ordered - but it made it hard to discern the taste. I also had a Longan juice, which was my first time. It was very refreshing and something I’d get again.

author: Jennifer Ruff
review_text: I was looking up late night spots in LA after getting some tattoos and this spot seemed pretty enticing! Although, in typical LA fashion the plaza is a mess for parking. There was a pretty sizable wait-list but the wait wasn't too bad. The food though? Delish!! Authentic, good portions and don't forget to order a side of rice and their locally brewed Ruen Pair beer.

author: Kavin Chan
review_text:
A mom-and-pop Thai restaurant, with a TV outside looping a video of their menu items. The owner explained that they immigrated to the US and couldn’t find any authentic Thai restaurants, so they decided to open their own. I found this a bit amusing, as many Thai and exotic restaurants are founded, and I doubt all of them are not authentic.

On my first night, I ordered the raw shrimp salad, which was good, but I think my stomach wasn’t reacting well to it. The next day, I tried something more popular and ordered the morning glory. It was good, but I wish they had added more chili to it.

The pad thai was great. It was served separately with bean sprouts and peanut crumbs. The dish wasn’t as sweet as other Thai restaurants, which I prefer. My order came with tofu, and it was generous. I highly recommend it.

author: Meecheer
review_text: Love this place so much! Authentic food and our favorite is the Shrimp cake. Sharing photos of take out meal from one of many times of our visits. Also sharing the parking rate sign at the parking lot.

author: Eric Cruz
review_text: Legend. That’s the best word to describe this place. I’ve been coming here since 1996 when they first opened and this place has become an LA institution for Thai food. Been to Thailand over 25x and this place is bonafide legit. Love how humble they remained even with the lines. They recently opened one of the best ice cream shops in the USA. This and Sanamluang down the street are my go to’s in Thai Town.

author: KG
review_text: This review has been a long time coming and it’s totally well deserved. I’ve been a loyal fan of Ruen Pair for over a decade now, ever since my Laotian friends from San Diego first introduced me to this gem of an authentic Thai spot. I don’t get to come here as often as I’d like since it’s kind of a trek from where I live, but best believe I make a stop every time I’m in LA. The food here is always on point, super consistent and packed with legit flavors that you just don’t get from your typical Americanized Thai restaurants. One quick way to tell it’s the real deal? Just look around at the crowd it says a lot about the kind of market this place caters to. This visit, we kept it classic. We started with the plain papaya salad you can’t go wrong with this dish. It’s super popular for a reason with generous portions and that perfect sweet-tangy-salty combo that sends me straight to Cloud 9. Next up was the Morning Glory, which is a must-have for me. It’s a simple vegetarian dish, but so flavorful and fresh. And to round it out, we got the Pad Woon Sen with shrimp balanced, tasty, and not heavy at all. It hits just right. If you’re in LA and find yourself near Thai Town, definitely make the stop. And trust me on this just pay for valet. Save yourself the parking stress. It’s worth it.

author: Derin
review_text: I’ve never been to a Thai restaurant with an hour wait on a Sunday, but I understand why. Probably the best Pad See Ew I’ve ever had.

author: Catlin Chase
review_text:
Absolutely loved this place! The food at Ruen Pair is incredibly authentic — the flavors are rich, balanced, and just the right level of spice. Everything tasted freshly made and full of that real Thai home-cooked vibe.

The staff were super friendly and welcoming from the moment we walked in, and our dishes came out surprisingly fast even though the restaurant was quite busy. You can really tell they care about both the food and the guests.

Highly recommend if you’re craving real Thai food in LA. Definitely coming back!

author: Laine
review_text: Always busy especially at peak hours like Friday night when we last had dinner here. We’ve been here numerous times and it never disappoints! Get the Pad See Ew, Papaya Salad, Crispy Egg Salad, Morning Glory, Pad Thai. Big family-size portions. Quick service. Just be prepared to wait! Parking is valet, cash only. Or you can try to find street parking.

author: Brent Cham
review_text:
Been here about 5x now and it’s one of my fave Thai places in LA.

The cons: parking in the area can be hard to find, sometimes there’s a wait, it’s not a place to have a long drawn out dinner (because it’s so popular but I’ve never felt rushed).

The pros: food is fantastic, lots of variety, even if there’s a wait it’s never that long, pretty standard pricing as well maybe even cheaper than some other Thai places.

Fave dishes: northern Thai sausage (insanely good), any of the curries, boat noodles.

Everything else is fantastic as well but those are the stand outs I’ve tried. Haven’t had one bad dish.

author: Liying Wu
review_text: Great authentic Thai food, Pork Leg over Rice is a must-try. Definitely will come again soon :)!

author: David D
review_text: Food is excellent, almost as good as my wife's cooking! This restaurant is ALWAYS busy. There is almost ALWAYS a line. So we always try to visit before 4pm, usually you can  get a table quickly. After 4pm it's a wait.  Food is spicy, not super salty, it's a rare treat, to have food actually prepared properly.  Bravo.

author: Joanne Sugiyama
review_text:
This is a no frills, small place but the food is LEGIT. My husband likes very spicy food and I like mine mild. We ended up sharing 3 plates and he added the dried chili peppers on the table to every single bite.
We had panang curry with chicken (spice level 1), pad see ew with beef and pad thai with beef.   The food came out fast and the flavor was on point!
We did have to wait a little bit at 8om on Friday night but the list went fast and we were seated, ate and walked over for gelato within 2 hours.
Highly recommend - we will be back!!!

author: M
review_text: Great good service and atmosphere obviously. Nobody asked but the waitstaff is cute too (respectfully). Seeing instant porridge /jok/juk/zhou on a grocery run made me realize it was an option so I looked and found they made it here — picked up with another recommended popular meal to make it easier — double win. Also it was do fast- they said 10-15 min and I came back from the sweets place across the lot to find it ready

author: J W
review_text:
This is my favorite thai restaurant in LA. I have been a long term customer here since 2018. Very authentic and delicious thai food, packed with flavors in my mouth.

Also, I am happy to see their prices are not inflated like crazy like other restaurants in 2025. You can tell this is a honest business with a loyal customer base.

P.s. The spicy raw shrimp is very spicy haha, but i love it! The sauce brings me back to Thailand.

author: JJ
review_text: Food is decent, but nothing special. I don’t think it’s worth the hype and the wait. Outside wait time for us was twice longer than the actual dining time. We were seated after 40 minutes. Waitress brought the check 15 mins after food is delivered. No water refill. $3 parking

author: Hencredible
review_text: One of my favorite Thai food restaurants in the area. Compared to southern Thai-style restaurants, this place has more natural flavor instead of using strong spices. Curries are more liquid, and fresh meat (dark meat) is used instead of more chewy breast meat. Expect some wait even at 5 p.m. on a Sunday, but the taste is worth it.

author: Ed Hendel
review_text: Fantastic pad see ew and morning glory. The crab fried rice and the spicy catfish were mediocre. There can be a long line if you come after 5pm.

author: Carrie Z
review_text:
My go-to spot for Sichuan cuisine takeout. The flavors are authentic, and dishes like the twice cooked pork are must-orders. It’s one of the few places my dad genuinely enjoys, which says a lot.

The restaurant is located right across the street from South Coast Plaza, in an area with many dining options. Whether you’re dining in or grabbing takeout, service is quick and reliable. It’s a small space, but there are plenty of tables. A hidden gem for real Sichuan flavor.

author: Sweta Baniya
review_text:
I had delicious vegan food here and both dishes were made with care! The owner also asked about Oyster sauce which I don’t eat! He was very attentive to my request and was very kind and careful.
The tofu was DELICIOUS! Cauliflower was okay!

author: Shelly Shi
review_text:
Updated: second time here with groups of friends. The dishes are authentic and big portions! Highly recommend.

Fast take out- the Szechuan cold noodles came out fast, and was delicious with tasty sauce, just wished there were some protein options can be added.

author: M planetmike
review_text: This is a Szechwan Zone. If you enjoy Spicy Chinese, this is the place. Like so many good restaurants in California, it is Innocuously located in a strip mall. We had excellent food and service. The restaurant furnishings have been updated. Prices were very reasonable. Our bill for 4 people came to $100. I encourage those who had negative experiences years ago to give this another chance.

author: Noa Pei
review_text: What a terrible dining experience! I was shocked to find hair in my food, and the indifferent tone and bad attitude of the waitress really shocked me. I really regret choosing to try the dishes here! It turns out that all those who gave bad reviews have their reasons! That waitress in the restaurant simply shouldn't be working in the service industry. She should be a queen at home!

author: Ben Park
review_text: Had the spicy cabbage, frog, and shrimp fried rice.  The fried rice was just ok, but the other two dishes were great.  The frog had a great texture and didn't taste fishy with a good numbing spice profile.  The cabbage was actually my favorite.  The staff was nice.  Order a Beijing yogurt.  It's just a sweet yogurt, but can offset the spice. EDIT: order the items with thumbs up. The spicy wontons and the garlic eggplant weren’t good but the items with thumbs up were good.

author: Kristine
review_text:
Tasty zone is a yummy spicy Chinese restaurant. Newly renovated dive covid it has a fun vibe. It's not a big restaurant so if you are coming at lunch or dinner hours there may be a wait. There is plenty of parking and well located in the shopping center at the corner.

The service is good. Nothing over the top but friendly and efficient.

The food is yummy and spicy. It is served hot and fresh. The menu is large with a huge variety to choose from spicy, ma la and not spicy. I recommend getting the yogurt if getting spicy if you are not used to it.

author: David Monson
review_text: Loved everything I ate here. Took me back to my year living in China. So flavorful. Soany of my favorite dishes. I'll be coming back for sure!

author: Carrie Menendez
review_text: Stopped in for unplanned lunch, amazing food with flavors and huge portions. Planning how to use our extras!

author: Andrew Z
review_text: One of the only good Chinese food places I have found. Their noodles are spectacular!

author: Jack Du
review_text:
Escape!!!

This place is a joke. Sure, the food might be ‘authentic,’ but the service is absolute garbage. One rushed, incompetent server for the whole restaurant, unable to follow simple order instructions, let alone refill water or provide napkins.

Worse, the server—a fellow Asian—was straight-up racist. Friendly and chatty with English speakers, but cold and monotone when I spoke Chinese. Unbelievable.

And the best part? When I rightfully chose not to tip for this disaster of a service, the server told me not to come back. Instead of whining about a missing tip, maybe ask yourself why you didn’t earn it in the first place.

Pathetic service, disrespectful staff—save your money and go somewhere that actually values customers.

author: Aisling Nox
review_text:
Would never recommend this place. If you’re ordering takeout, be prepared to wait A LONG time past their time they tell you it’s ready. Also double check your order before you walk away. They’ll sometimes just “forget” a dish.
So if you order takeout add on at least 15+ minutes to their estimated time.

You’ll be waiting 30+ minutes and they won’t tell you anything about how much longer. They won’t even offer you a cup of water. Absolute zero sense of customer service. Not an ounce of thanks for waiting or sorry for the delay. Food is mediocre at best. Just drive to Irvine and get your Szechuan fix. Beware. Also, I’m pretty sure they reuse their oil day after day. Pretty shocked the food inspector hasn’t shut them down. Never again.

author: Xueting Alford
review_text: Had this meal last Thursday. Everything was great! Especially the service! The waitor was very considerate and sweet!

author: charlie purdue
review_text: driest chinese food i have ever had. was burnt black, had almost no sauce, no side of rice or vegetables to add flavor... portions were also offensively small for $18... girl at the counter was quick but not very friendly, not that i care, since i will not be coming back

author: Stacy Feinberg
review_text: We have been going here for years now, it is amazing! So so so delicious! One of my favorite foods. It’s hard to describe how amazing the taste and quality is. My favorite item on the menu is spicy wonton.please go here! It’s amazing

author: Kuang Yueheng
review_text: On Wednesday, I went to Tasty zone with my husband for dinner. This is a restaurant my husband and I often visit. We like their food very much. My husband and I like almost every dish, including rice noodles, jelly noodles and cold dishes. The restaurant is beautiful and clean, and the service is very good. In particular, the Sichuan cuisine made by their chef is very authentic and flavorful. I think it is the best Sichuan cuisine in Costa Mesa and I never get tired of it.

author: Angel Kim
review_text:
I wanted to order the dry pot but it wasn’t vegetarian. The waiter offered to change the meat into veggies with fried tofu. IT WAS SUPER GOOD and it is big! I’d definitely come back again for the dry pot.

Eggplant w/ garlic sauce was good too!

author: Peter B
review_text:
This place is authentic and delicious food. These other reviews are absolute trash and mostly lies, written by delusional Karens with no idea what Sichuan food is. People saying they had allergic reactions when the numbing peppercorns are literally foundational to Sichuan cuisine.

This place is great. Don't listen to the dumbos. Get the beans and spicy chicken.

author: Matthew Walker
review_text: Trust me, take the highway to the Tasty Zone!!  For those of you who are familiar with Szechwan food and it’s unique flavors, you’ll be so happy that you finally found THE place.  The quality, portions, prices, spiciness/numbing—it’s all just so wonderful.

author: Calvin
review_text: I came here about 10 years ago several times.  And it is still here.  The dishes are still delicious and in good portions.  Wish you the best and stay another 10 years.

author: Yvonne A
review_text:
We absolutely loved our visit to Ipoh Kopitiam!Everything was so delicious and packed with that authentic Malaysian flavor we’ve been craving. The nasi hainam was incredibly tender and fragrant, the dry wanton mee was perfectly seasoned, and the sambal had the right amount of kick. Even the Milo drink tasted just like home!

We’re already missing Ipoh’s food, and of course we’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended for anyone looking for real, comforting Malaysian flavors! 🍜🇲🇾✨

author: Yasmeen Wilde
review_text: The best and most authentic Malaysian food I ever had in the United States. Ipoh kopitiam is a famous chain in Malaysia. I am so happy when I found out they opened a store in Alhambra. We had the chicken rice, kway teow noodles and roti canai. All amazing. The place is always crowded and service is quick. There was a waitlist but it went by super quick.

author: AJ
review_text:
We ordered the Singapore Curry Laksa, Rendang Curry Beef, Kaya Toast, and White Coffee.
Everything was absolutely delicious especially the Rendang Curry Beef, which was insanely good.

I’ve been to Singapore about twelve times, and the Laksa here tasted just like what I had there.

The interior also really reminded me of cafes in Singapore and Malaysia — cozy, casual, and authentic. Definitely worth visiting if you miss Southeast Asian flavors.

author: Linda Pham
review_text: Delicious food! Seems like there's a long line during the day but we ate around 8pm with little to no line. The Hainan chicken is our favorite! Meat is super tender and soft and the sauces provided are delicious. We also loved the Kaya toast and butter. Can't beat the classics! Parking is available underground behind the building.

author: Judy Nie
review_text: Amazing Malaysian/Singaporean food! Came here for the breakfast sets. Price is so reasonable! A set comes with entree + hot drink + side. Tried the curry noodles, kaya butter toast, and hot milk tea. Everything was on point and authentic! Also impeccable service, they offered us refills for the milk tea. You have to come here for breakfast!

author: Anonymous
review_text: Very authentic Hainan chicken rice and laksa even better than places in SG and Malaysia. Outdoor seating is warm and cozy. Long wait but food is excellent.

author: Felisia Micky
review_text:
One cozy place for breakfast with delicious meals they serve is Ipoh Kopitiam.
They got breakfast menu with affordable price until 10.45am. The price start $12.95++ for menu A and $13.95++ for menu B.
I attached the menu which you can choose. First you choose the main course such as nasi lemak or noodle soup which is both are super recommended, the you choose the topping you want which is i love the spam, then the bread (toast) which is i recommended is the toast with Kaya and butter. This included choice of drinks which you can get freeflow, such as hot coffee, hot milk tea, hot chinese tea or hot lemon tea for cold (ice) got extra charge for $ 1.50.

No wonder they got michelin bib gourmand since 2022! Super duper recommended.

author: Lingyu Liu
review_text:
Finally made it to Ipoh Kappitiam, and it absolutely hit the spot. Everything tasted warm, familiar, and full of that cozy Southeast Asian comfort.

i ordered Hainan Chicken Rice
The chicken was tender and silky, just the way it should be. The rice was fragrant and perfectly oily, and the trio of sauces—ginger, chili, and dark soy—tied everything together. Simple but so satisfying.

author: J L
review_text:
Second time lucky as there's usually a very long wait here. The virtual waiting queue helps as you can't book!

I grew up in Malaysia and Laksa is my go to. My broth was rich from the coconut milk, fragrant from the spices and umami from the shrimp and curry flavours. The noodles were different from the mix of Hokkien noodles with Vermicelli I'm used to, but still chewy and contrasted with the textures of the other ingredients.
My friend's Bak Kut Teh (pork ribs in herb soup) were tough and dry, like the meat is overcooked. The ratings reflect this chewing exercise for her jaw.

Service was very efficient as we would expect for such a busy place. The front patio increased the seating area and the whole place was bustling. They didn't kick us out as soon as we finish, which would be very common in many countries. Maybe this is because of the tipping culture?

author: Vu Tran
review_text:
A place worth visiting and enjoying exotic Asian food.
The exotic food is delicious, the service is attentive, the atmosphere is moderate and not too noisy.
Will come back next time, and recommend this place to friends.

author: satsuki hoshino
review_text:
We came here to sign up the queue and found out that you could just do it by yelp’s app for faster seating.  Mostly seating are for two or four. There seems a section that could accommodate larger party like 5 or 6 people. A lot of families came too.

We already came couple times before. It actually has been our favorite place for laksa noodle soup. I like its flavorful soup and very bouncy noodle texture. Also included a lot of fried tofu boiled egg shrimp and fish balls.

We had already tried stew beef with bread so this time we tried fried beef with wide rice noodles also sweet buns with butter. Both were great. For drinks you could customize the sugar levels.

Our favorite dish is fried chicken wings in peppercorn and salt flavors.

Also waiters were always friendly and courteous. The only things was it could be a bit of noisy since everyone was talking loudly and sometimes seating was very close.

author: Carl Wong
review_text: Came here for lunch. I've been when it first opened, since then they had picked up 3 Michelin Bib Gourmand awards. This is a nice Malaysian comfort food café, so don't expect immaculate service. The staff is very nice, friendly and multi lingual. The food, however, is excellent. I ordered the Roti Cenai and Hainan chicken rice (to go) and the Hokkien Prawn noodle soup and Malaysian milk tea for dining in. The broth is amazing, the noodles are not soggy, the water spinach (kangkung) is fresh and crisp and the shrimp is good as well. It seems the Hainan chicken rice is rather popular. Will find out how it compares to Savoy. I got seated right away, however as I was leaving there was a line outside at 1pm.

author: Vivian “Vivventure” Wayfarer
review_text:
Authentic Malaysian/Singaporean breakfast spot with great combo prices (12-15 bucks for a set with an entree, a drink - all kinds of kopi, and complementary pastry of choice — ranging from Kaya toast, pandan cake, to pineapple buns). We ordered three sets, giving us a chance to try instant noodles with curry pork skin, nasi lemak with curry fish balls and Malaysian sticky rice with chicken. All the dishes hit the spot and are reminiscent of what you would get in the region locally.

Definitely need to come back to try the lunch, which seems to be popular!

author: Sabs A
review_text: Ipoh Kopitiam in Alhambra is a great spot for authentic Southeast Asian flavors that are hard to find in California. The roti was easily my favorite dish - crispy, flaky, and absolutely delicious. The wantan mee with curry chicken was very tasty and especially nostalgic, reminding me of my trips to Singapore, though I would’ve loved the option for boneless chicken or BBQ pork instead. The beef rendang was flavorful and rich, with a noticeable kick of spice. Service was genuinely excellent - friendly, attentive, and often anticipating our needs - and while pricing was decent, the generous portions meant we happily took leftovers home.

author: B L
review_text:
My go-to spot for authentic Hainan chicken rice and white coffee! This restaurant never fails to deliver - the chicken is always tender, flavorful, and perfectly poached. The rice is fragrant and infused with just the right amount of chicken stock.

And the white coffee? Divine! Smooth, creamy, and not too sweet. It's the perfect complement to their delicious Hainan chicken.

The service is always friendly, and the atmosphere is cozy and welcoming. If you're a fan of Hainan chicken or great coffee, this spot is a must-visit!

author: William Fong
review_text:
For all the hype and wait, I was extremely disappointed.  I thought it would stand out but everything we ordered was only OK.

The Portuguese tart taste like bought from elsewhere and heated up.

San Francisco cafes like this is way better.

That is the honest truth.

author: Dee Jay
review_text: First time visiting and one thing to know! Join the waitlist before you actually get here!! We didn’t know and waited two hours 🥲But the food didn’t disappoint me. We tried their laksa noodle, chicken curry, Kaya butter toast and roti! Everything was on point and delicious! I love their Kaya and Butter toast. It’s so simple but so flavorful ❤️

author: Riki Yamashita
review_text:
Wah lao weh! It definitely is like home, Ipoh mali. Delicious just like from my childhood. Authentic Malaysian Hainanese Chicken Rice. The closest I recall tastes as good as in PJ's Japan Gasing (near SFX Church) or Subang Jaya's SS15. My friend flew it from LA to Pittsburgh. It was an amazing treat.

When I visit LA, this place would be my destination.

author: K
review_text:
Came here during a holiday and was able to get seated quickly during tea time.
I got the Singapore style hainan chicken and rice and Malaysian style BBQ pork and rice. Both dishes were delicious. For the drinks, I ordered the hot lemon tea and milk tea. Both teas were good.  The milk tea came in small teacup and was on the heavy side. They refill on these. They have heaters if you are seated outdoors, which was great.
I'm glad I got to try this place out. The customer service is great. The restaurant is nice, clean and cozy. Overall, I enjoyed my experience here.

I can't wait to come back during dinner time since the menu changes.

Free street parking.

author: Andy Mai
review_text: This restaurant is Michelin Guide 2024 and it definitely deserves it. The food doesn't have plenty of selection but everything is very tasty. You can try everything and it will taste good. The toast is what you should try as dessert instead of appetizers since it's pretty sweet and perfect after a meal. Plenty of parking in the parking structure behind the plaza. Seats can be limited so expect a wait line. Once you are in, the food comes out pretty fast. It's a handicap friendly facility.

author: Megan Gomez-Reyes
review_text: There is hardly any Potato Corner locations in LA Metropolitan area, so when we saw this location, we came out here for a nice quick bite. We had Spicy BBQ Loopy fries with the chicken tenders, and Garlic and Parmesan Loopy fries with tenders as well. The chicken is amazing, and the fries weren't bad but maybe we will try different flavors next time. It would be nice if they had a Cajun flavor or regular seasoned salt, though. But no complaints, but for a place called Potato Corner, the star of the show was definitely the chicken. Nice and hot, and REALLY crunchy!

author: Shawn Sheng
review_text: The different flavors of fries just hit different. They are super tasty and cause a flavor explosion in your mouth. Their chicken wings are decent too. A nice spot to go to after walking around the Americana for a snack. Nice and simple fast food. Make sure to enjoy while it is hot.

author: Rose
review_text: potato corner is for sure the best place to get fries. their sour cream flavor is simply addicting. i would come back to it over and over again if i could!

author: David Karapetyan
review_text: The worker didn’t want to get my order because of the personal conflict with one of my friends. So I do not suggest to go there, the worker has some mental and personal problems. I would rate a negative number but I just put 1 star because I cant put less than that.

author: Nicole A
review_text: Made by people that clearly have never tasted real potato corner bc what is up with the seasoning?? Yall just dump a whole bag in there or something? The ingredients are all there you just have to make it right. Also prices are outrageous patatas lang naman toh pero lahat di marunong.

author: Kevin Santos
review_text: Potato Corner is the best flavored fries at the best location! Sometimes this is our only reason to visit Americana. 😂

author: sisi
review_text: Please bring back the old Potato Corner and the original staff—this new setup just isn’t it. The experience has gone downhill. The cashier was fine, but the girl who handed me my food was incredibly rude. Seriously, someone needs to address her attitude. It’s disappointing to see how much the service has changed.

author: casual gamer
review_text:
I occasionally stop by Potato Corner at the Americana, usually about once or twice every two months, for a quick bite. I’m not a regular customer, so the staff doesn’t recognize me. Unfortunately, the service has been consistently disappointing every time I’ve visited.

While I’m not a big fan of wings or chicken tenders, I do enjoy the food from Potato Corner. However, the lack of customer service leaves a lot to be desired. The staff, who seem to be fresh out of high school, never acknowledge me when I pick up my order. They simply hand it over without so much as a “thank you,” even when I make the effort to thank them first.

It’s clear that the young employees lack the work ethic and customer service skills necessary for this job. It’s frustrating as a customer to be treated with indifference, especially when all I’m doing is ordering food. A little politeness and appreciation can go a long way, but unfortunately, that’s been missing every time I’ve visited.

author: reshy daswani
review_text: January 31 around 7:30-8:30pm - Bad star for the woman with curly hair here. I ordered my childhood favorite bbq giga fries. The fries barely had seasoning so I asked her to give me a bit of bbq powder and she rudely said that it costs 50 cents. At that point, I did not have my card with me because my friend was sitting far away watching my stuff and it was very cold but she did not cared when I told her that. The Asian woman with fair skin ended up helping and she was friendly. She was pleasant and offered a good service.

author: JOYN
review_text: Went on November 3 2023 at 4:30 pm . Woman working the counter was extremely rude. I stood in line for almost half an hour just to get up to the front and have them tell me they’re out of most items . I would think a sign saying that they’re out of food would be appropriate which I kindly let her know. she then told me “oh we’ll get over it” I’m literally in shock

author: A
review_text: Delicious flavored French fries can’t speak for the rest of the food or drinks but the French fries are yummy.

author: Keith Patch (Patches)
review_text: It's a quaint little place to get fries and chicken tenders. It's not amazing, but it's a good amount of food for the price.

author: Armen B
review_text: My kids love this place. For adults it is little greasy but kids love French fries.

author: Berge Wassilian
review_text: For a quick fill of your stomach: French fries - Fast and delicious.

author: Polina Shevchenko
review_text: A variety of potato options, and you can customize it just the way you like. Delicious. Thank you!

author: Arno Harutyunyan
review_text: This Place Is A Very Good Place To Eat.The Food Is Good.The Service Is Good.And The Workers Are Very Nice.Keep Up The Great Work!

author: Armen Hovhannisyan
review_text: Something has changed about the food here, the chicken tenders seem different like a cheaper quality and the fries taste bland.

author: Adam Lambert
review_text: God they have 1 place to take peoples order and it takes them 45 minutes to take 1 persons order. 0 stars don’t waste your time

author: Evelyn Garcia
review_text: Worst unsanitary place ever!! Bought my kids some fries here and they both got food poisoning. Worst experience of my life witnessing my toddlers 2 year old and 3 year old having diarrhea, throwing up, screaming in pain, shaking and sweating from this. Never again will I buy from here. Please clean your stuff or wash your hands make everything so this won’t happen to anyone else or any kids since every kid loves fries. The feeling as a mother to not be able to do anything and see your kids in pain is the worst feeling ever.

author: hector cordero
review_text:
Saturday 3 22 2025 I ordered tatter tots with extra cheddar and when I smelled and tasted the food it was rancid. The powder being used smelled like it has been in a plastic container for a very long time and expired. I ended trashing the food as I was already far from the location. We were looking forward to the tater. Tots, unfortunately the expectation, what's i'm not there. Please have your staff trained on your product and even taste the product and have knowledge of what is old, What is rancid and what should be served.

Thank you
Hector Cordero
F&B Assist Director CSUN

author: Jeff Tomasich
review_text:
The ultimate LA brunch splurge.

République never misses. We came for a New Year's brunch and everything was outstanding.

Highlights:
The Food: We ordered the brisket burrito, lobster omelette, and the famous brioche French toast. All three were excellent—no misses.

The Vibe: Great energy, beautiful interior, and the perfect place for a special occasion meal.
It remains a top-tier brunch destination in the city. Expect a line, but know that the food is worth the wait.

author: Ayidh AlQahtani
review_text:
It offers a wonderful dining experience from start to finish. The atmosphere is beautiful and lively with a great mix of elegance and comfort that makes the place feel special yet welcoming. The vibes are perfect for breakfast or brunch.

The food was outstanding. The waffle was incredibly delicious and full of flavor. The shakshuka was just as impressive, rich and well-seasoned, with perfectly cooked eggs and fresh ingredients. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared and satisfying.

Overall, République combines great food, excellent service and an amazing atmosphere. It’s a place I would happily return to and confidently recommend to anyone looking for a memorable dining experience.

author: Ken Wong
review_text:
December 2025:
Excellent restaurant. Came here for dinner and was very pleased with my meal.

Started with the Le Menuier butter 🧈 and bread. Highlight of the meal. Superb butter! Would definitely come back again for this dish!

We also had the endive salad, pork belly, NY strip steak 🥩. All three dishes were very tasty 😋.

Got the strawberry 🍓 tiramisu for dessert. A delicious finale of a great meal.

Service was friendly and attentive. Looking forward to coming back again.

author: Mayank Dayal
review_text:
République

Absolutely loved this place, and it truly lives up to the reputation it has built across Los Angeles as one of the city’s most iconic French cafés. From the moment you walk in, the space feels special, a beautiful blend of historic charm and modern Parisian energy. The atmosphere is warm, buzzing, and full of life, though it can definitely get fairly busy, especially during peak brunch hours. That said, the energy only adds to the experience.

The seasonal egg nog was fantastic, rich, balanced, and comforting, clearly made with care and attention to detail. The French toast was the real standout, absolutely outstanding and deserving of all the love it gets online. The inside was unbelievably soft and buttery, while the outside had the most awesome crisp, light crunch, with just the right amount of fluff throughout. It’s one of those dishes you keep thinking about long after the meal is over.

The French omelette was also excellent, perfectly cooked, creamy, and delicate, exactly how a classic French omelette should be. Simple, elegant, and deeply satisfying.

Overall, République is one of those rare places that manages to deliver on both food and experience. It’s easy to see why it’s consistently recommended by locals and visitors alike. Busy, yes, but absolutely worth it. A place you’ll want to return to, again and again.

author: Alicia Roman
review_text: This is an amazing and unique place has kind of a historic authentic vibe, grabbed coffee & a pastry first, then ended up staying longer than planned and got a salmon toast that was excellent. The bakery case is dangerous (in a good way), service was busy and need to improve, yet they were friendly, and everything tasted fresh. Would happily come back.

author: Joaquín Ferretti Matta
review_text:
I left a bit disappointed. I came in with high expectations for the pastries—especially the croissants—but they fell short for me. I’ve been to many bakeries with a wider variety (think pistachio, Nutella, etc.), larger size, and similar pricing. The quality didn’t quite match what I was hoping for, especially considering the cost.

That said, the atmosphere is absolutely beautiful. The indoor seating genuinely feels like you're sitting in a European café, which I loved. The coffee was excellent, and the savory dishes were delicious—just keep in mind they are very pricey. For reference, two pastries, two coffees, and two main dishes came out to $115 including tip. Definitely on the higher end.

Overall, I’m glad I tried it and it was a nice experience, but I’m not sure I’d return—at least not for the pastries. If you’re looking for a great croissant, this wouldn’t be my first choice right now. But for ambiance and coffee, it’s worth experiencing at least once.

author: John kozman
review_text:
I’ve heard so much about République Café and was honestly worried it might be overrated — but it definitely isn’t. I tried the crab omelette, and it’s hands-down the best omelette I’ve ever had. Perfect texture, rich flavor, and worth every bit of the hype.

The only downside: the staff seemed a bit sad or low-energy. Not rude, just not as warm as you’d expect in a place this good.

Food: 10/10
Atmosphere: Great
Service: Could be happier

author: David Lee
review_text:
I’ve lived in LA for almost 25 years seven of those right in Miracle Mile near République and it remains one of the absolute top restaurants in the city. It’s our go-to spot whenever we have guests visiting from out of town or overseas, and they always fall in love with it, too.

Everything is consistently on point. Too many favorites to list. The coffee and pastries are outstanding, and the food is always exceptional. I also really love the vibe the energy, the mood, the music, it all just works. Service is excellent every time.

We went a few days ago, and the woman at the pastry counter was incredibly kind. She later came by our table and asked how our first bite was… and honestly, it was delicious. République never misses!!

author: prezelonline
review_text:
Ambiance ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Loved the space. The large glass windows bring in so much natural light, and knowing this used to be Chaplin’s office gives it extra character. The sunlight coming through the glass ceiling is absolutely beautiful — it instantly puts you in a good mood.🥰.

Food ⭐⭐⭐⭐
The food was solid. The shakshuka and mushroom toast were standard. The potato pancake was a pleasant surprise — crispy on the outside with a soft, fluffy interior. The Basque cheesecake was definitely above average and nicely done.

Overall ⭐⭐⭐⭐½
The food is good, but the ambiance really steals the show here. It does get quite busy on weekends, which takes away a bit from the experience. I imagine coming here on a weekday, sitting in the sun, would feel especially relaxing and lovely.

author: Kent Burke
review_text: This was my first time visiting here. We decided to come here for a team dinner after a work event based on the recommendation of one of our colleagues. It was well worth the experience. The food was delicious, and everyone seemed to enjoy the variety of dishes that we ordered. I will say that it was my first time having a dish with white truffles — it wasn’t my favorite dish of the evening, even though everyone else seemed to thoroughly enjoy it. I would definitely recommend giving this place a try if you are in the area.

author: Martina Sora
review_text:
The pastries are amazing and truly delicious, and the coffee is very good as well. The atmosphere has nice vibes.

However, the matcha wasn’t great, and the brunch/breakfast dishes didn’t meet expectations. The eggs were watery, and we were told we had to pay extra to get more bread, which felt a bit disappointing. The salad was also not well balanced, as it was overly watery due to the added fruit like mandarins and grapefruit.

Overall, I’d recommend sticking to pastries and coffee, as that’s where this place really shines. The service could be improved too—the waiters seemed a bit unhappy and not very friendly.

author: Ari A.
review_text:
Firstly, do not part at the lot, it’s minuscule and $14 for brunch timing parking is steep.

The lines were long but it moved quickly. You are quickly overwhelmed with the amount of pastry choices and very little time to decide.

Once you picked out your pastries, you’re able to order your entrées at the cashier and pay for your food. They give you a number and then off you go walking through the entire restaurant looking for a table. In our case, it was standing around waiting for someone to get up.

The restaurant was full and yet they refused to open up the second floor for patrons. Our food arrived, and we still didn’t have a table to sit in, which was frustrating.

The five of us squeezed into a two top until a larger table was available. Once we were done with our meal, I noticed there were tables that were empty that were for dirty plates that were not cleared in time.

The food was good but for the service and price for valet, would not recommend unless you were looking specifically to overpay for next to no service.

author: Rick Smith
review_text: The menu had a lot of amazing choices, and walking around while snooping…there were several breakfast choices and I kinda wish I ordered a couple of different ones.  I chose the regular breakfast, and it was good.  The bacon was really thick, which was a new experience for me.  A note for future reviewers…the food menu should be loaded way more than the drink menu, cmon people.  I had to click on the 5th picture under menus to see food!

author: Dusko Vuksanovic
review_text: I just checked it off my bucket list. And it didn’t disappoint. The food is great as the decor. Just amazing place. Must visit if in LA. Waiting time for brunch can be a bit long, but well worth it!

author: Chris Shaul
review_text:
We've been wanting to try this place for some time, but finally got her today.

We parked in the valet (as there was no street parking) and went in.  The entry area is small and we were there at 11:30am and most of the pastries were sold out.  (get there early for the full selection)

We studied the menu and ordered a couple of pasteries first.  That is how it works, you order your pastry selections from the case, while waiting in line for the cashier to take your food order.  We ordered a donut hole-like item that had a cream filling and a Passion Fruit cream cake.   For our food, we ordered a Cuban Sandwich and the Adobo Pork Fried Rice. My wife ordered a cafe mocha and I appreciated that my iced tea was with bergamot.

We took our table number (which was an old beat up tin cup - kind of fun) and found a table.  We were seated right at the indoor archways to the back dining room.  I enjoyed looking at the classic cathederal-like architecture while dining.

Our food came and it was really good.  I had the Cuban Sandwich and it was probably the best I've every had.  My wife enjoyed her fried rice, but we both loved my salad that came with the sandwich. It was the best thing in the meal!  It was simple butter lettuce, but the home made dressing was unbelievably good, with fresh herbs.

We also enjoyed the desserts we ordered, but I was more impressed with the lunch items.  That said the cream pie was tasty.

We will be back as there are so many more dishes I'd like to try.

author: Mohamed AlQubaisi
review_text:
You got to try their food to be honest. It’s just tasty and we went for breakfast. Avocado toast with scrambled egg on side and the egg Benedict with salmon (which was delicious).
We came early morning which I would recommend to avoid the crowds which they got busy quickly.
Note: it’s a bit pricy in my opinion but worth every dollars

author: Kirby Ong
review_text:
Kimchi fried rice was very delicious tho it was slightly expensive.

Brioche was also really good, along with both the coffee and hot chocolate.

Atmosphere was chill with plenty of people around, come before the main meal times to get a seat without waiting too long

author: Shawn Sheng
review_text: No wonder this place is one of the most popular spots in all of LA. During the day they operate as a cafe and amazing brunch spot, and in the evening become a fancy dinner restaurant. The bakery selection is incredible, and everything looks so good. They also have a regular menu with food and drink options. The interior is one of the most beautiful I have ever seen, grand architecture and plenty of space in a bustling environment. Despite the chaos they keep things very efficient and operating smoothly. The food was wonderful, everything we got was delicious. Definitely worth checking out, be sure to go early to avoid a long wait time.

author: G Fong
review_text: Went for Sunday brunch.  10am.  There was a long line in front.  May 15 groups back.  Took about 15 min to get to the front.  There is one line for to go and one for pastries and food.  We ordered 4 pastries and 2 meals.  Filipino Adobo fried rice and short rib burrito.  Both very good.  Lots of seating inside and out.

author: Seth Horton
review_text: I don’t understand how this place has any negative reviews because this was the highlight of my time in California. I ate breakfast here and they had the best selection of pastries. We ordered breakfast and sat down, everything came out fast and the service was on point. We ordered the brisket burrito and the potato pancake and a couple pastries and I was in heaven. I hope I can stop by on my return flight. 10/10

author: may
review_text: Hands down the best late night hearty meal after a fun night with friends! The food regardless of what you choose is amazing with fresh ingredients and full of flavor! The employees have it down and are so quick to assist and are friendly. It does get quite busy depending on when you go, but since SND closes so late there tends to be a wait at night. There’s plenty of tables and the workers do their best with the waitlist. Parking is limited, so your best bet is street parking. Def my go to late meal spot or hangover meal! :)

author: Ariel L
review_text:
We’ve been to this restaurant countless times, but today’s takeout experience was extremely disappointing. When I arrived to pick up the order, the staff had already tied the bag tightly and simply pushed it to me for payment. When we got home, we discovered the entire meal had a burnt taste — including the potatoes and rice cakes.

We called the restaurant, and they told us we should have checked the food at pickup. How were we supposed to check it when you tied the bag in a tight knot? And how can anyone see or smell a burnt taste through photos?

To-go portions are also significantly smaller than dining in.

I absolutely do not recommend this place, especially for to-go orders.

author: Ashley Z
review_text:
Came here during the holidays and had to wait about an hour, but honestly — totally worth it. The beef short rib stew was incredibly tender, falling apart with every bite, and I loved that it wasn’t overly seasoned. Just pure, rich flavor.

The dramatic fire show was everything — definitely added some emotional value to the meal! 🔥🧀
Great food, fun experience. Would absolutely come back!

author: Levent Arslan
review_text: This place is super popular! The food is delicious, especially the soup! I came late at night, and there were lots of sexy and pretty girls eating here; they seemed to have just come from nightclubs.

author: D L
review_text: This is such a great restaurant. If you love Korean soups this is the place for you. Their sul long tang is amazing. The sides dishes are traditional and go perfect with the soups. The service is fast and attentive, they refill them without asking. The hot tea is free and soothing. It’s big inside and even when fill doesn’t feel cramped. And did I mention it’s open 24 hours? The also have specials before 10:30am.

author: Calvin Xu
review_text: There was a very long line to get in; however it moved relatively quickly we ended up waiting 20ish minutes. The line outside is confusing but there is a line for smaller groups and one for larger groups. There is no wait-list you just have to stand in line. The food was excellent, a bit bland for my taste but ultimately very good.

author: JUSTIN CHEN 俊佳
review_text: Had a solid expectation before coming in. We're from greater NY area so we were exposed to a lot of good Korean food like fort lee, and cho dan gols in ktown. This place is just disappointing for me, small plates were lacking variety and taste, not even 1/5 as good as cho dan gol. It feels like a touristy spot. We got the medium side beef plate with no cheese, this dish is decent and over portioned for 2.  But I do like the taste however it was a pretty darn heavy and sauce dependent dish.

author: Yeojin Choi
review_text:
It was my first time here with my friends, and the Galbijjim was amazing 😭
Huge thanks to our server, Luna - the service was outstanding!

author: Richard Wehmeyer
review_text:
Good Korean restaurant with many soup options. This restaurant is also good for groups. We’ve seen many orders of a shared dish that is covered with cheese and gets melted with a little fire show. We’ve ordered no. 5 and no. 12. Both was delicious, good size.
For a Tuesday evening it was pretty full.
Valet Parking is $4

author: Si Chen
review_text: The food is fabulous! We ordered the braised beef short rib and ox tail. It’s a spicy and a bit sweet even my two kids loved it. Service is great too! Will definitely come back soon!

author: Gary C
review_text:
Amazing Sulung Tang. The soup was deep flavorful ox bone broth. They give a lot of meats too! The side dishes were fresh.

There is parking here and it was $2 even if we park ourselves. And the service boy yelled at us for entering at the side door by the parking?! But otherwise good place to eat.

author: Mingxi Xu (Ming)
review_text:
I’ve been missing Sun Nong Dan ever since my first visit two years ago, and this time I literally flew all the way from London just to eat here again! The food is absolutely unforgettable.

Special thanks to Jun, who made our experience even better with his friendly service. If you come here, definitely ask for him~~

Highly recommend!

author: li xiaoqi
review_text: Really delicious. Luna is so sweet to tell us which one is the most famous one. The food is awesome, and you can choose the level of spicy

author: Sheenu Chirakel
review_text: By golly! This place, this food, Luna, I have left speechless and tummy full. Luna’s SPEEDY service allowed me to enjoy QUALITY time with my friends. Luna really makes this place-I heard she owns the restaurant! Los Angeles would be proud. I would fly back with my friend Nitisha just for this!

author: Denise Cerezo
review_text: First time eating here after spending the whole day in an amusement park last month with my friends. We finished really late and it's one of the few restaurants that is open. The hot beef soup hit the spot with its vegetables. The flavor is very mild  so if you are used to seasoned food this place is not for you. They also have an array of side dishes. You can also get a refill of soup if your hotpot dries up. They have paid parking which is okay since it's a bit dangerous late at night.

author: Minghao shi
review_text: Pretty good overall. The hot pot is enough for 3–4 people, and we finished it in two rounds. Price is fair and the servers are super nice.

author: Dannie Qing
review_text:
Unfortunately, our experience here was disappointing, mainly due to service issues.

While we were waiting in line, customers who arrived after us were seated first, which felt unfair and poorly managed. During takeout preparation, staff placed the takeout containers on the bench between our table and the neighboring table, packing food right next to us — essentially beside our seats — which felt uncomfortable and unprofessional.

Additionally, the final amount charged appeared to be calculated based on the post-tax total, which was confusing and unexpected.

The wait was extremely long, and while the food was acceptable, it was not memorable enough to justify the overall experience. We likely won’t be returning.

author: Namuunaa Tsagaanbaatar
review_text: My favorite place to eat out. Jun is super fun and helpful! I love everything about this place, the food is always delicious, the vibe is upbeat, and the staff are super friendly. It’s the kind of spot that makes you want to come back again and again. The only thing is the music can get a little loud sometimes, but honestly, it just adds to the lively atmosphere.

author: George Sharrard
review_text:
Oh boy!  What a meal.  After flying from Orlando to LA with many delays I was starved.  My local LA buddy recommended SYD, so that is where we went.
We each had #10s.  Some kind of beef soup.  Super good!
It is noisy and feels crowded.

(sorry about the upside down menu picture...

author: Andrew Cervantes
review_text: Best Galbi Jjim I've ever had! Spicy level was just right. Side dishes were amazing, thank you to our server Luna.

author: ZX Tan
review_text: Truly one of the best meals I’ve had in my life. This is on par with what I’ve had in Jeju and even better than food I’ve had in Seoul. Service was warm and friendly as well. Only thing to take note is that the servings are HUGE and you need to order one set per person. The amount and quality of food is totally worth the price you pay for.

author: Bryan Kwon
review_text:
Time of visit - 11am Wednesday

Order - course meal ($35 per person) at least 2 people needed. Would not recommend this place if you intend to dine alone. Portions are large.

Food - every single dish reminds me of rural South Korea. I loved every single dish down to the last drop of plum dessert drink. If you haven’t had food from rural Korea, you may find the food here bland with unfamiliar flavors so this place cannot be enjoyed by everyone. But if you remember the taste of grandma cooking back in Korea you would love this place.

Service is excellent when the place is not full of people. The most popular menu item is the course meal so expect delays when the place is packed.

author: Julie Kim
review_text: I'm glad I tried it, but don't feel compelled to visit again. We arrived just past noon and our rice arrived room temp, our soups quickly reached room temp, and the entire meal felt very rushed and not particularly special given the high cost/person. As mentioned previously, the food quality reminded me of a Korean school cafeteria! That said, the ladies who work there are very kind and nice. Parking in the small shared lot behind the restaurant can be a challenge.

author: Marie Kang-Scott
review_text: My friends wanted to try authentic Korean food, so we went to Borit Gogae, which had a 4.3 Google rating. The restaurant is spacious, decorated with traditional Korean items, and even has goods available for purchase. For dinner, we ordered the “Banchan” set with barley rice ($29.99 per person), which included soybean soup and chicken soup. We also had to order a meat or fish dish separately, so we went with the LA Kalbi and yellow corvina. Unfortunately, the banchan and both soups were very bland—I didn’t eat them. The Kalbi was tasty, but the corvina was so nasty I couldn’t finish even one bite. The service was good, but overall, I wouldn’t return.

author: Michael Pinto
review_text:
I was really excited to try this place after seeing it all over social media and YouTube. Overall, I’d give it a 3/5. The service and atmosphere were great, but when it came down to the main reason we came—to enjoy the food—it fell short considering the price.

We ordered the 보리밥정식 set at $34.99 per person, which came with a variety of side dishes and porridge. I knew it would be centered around side dishes, but nothing really stood out or left a lasting impression.

For two people, the total came to about $77 before tip, and roughly $93 after. For that price, it feels like a bit of a splurge for what you get—I think you’d get a more satisfying meal (and value) at a Korean BBQ spot for around the same cost.

author: Ann Lee
review_text: Second time visiting today. There is a wow factor when you go the first time because of the way dishes are presented. But nothing to rave about. You would think soybean soup is a korean staple and can't mess up, but was so bland and diluted with water. And tofu cut to micro cubes. I eat very bland but this was just flavorless. Almost thought due to inflation are they saving their denjang to stretch as much as possible! And the chicken stew is grits plus some chicken legs thrown in. Even grits out of the box is gritty and souplike. Today's was off like diluted reheated grits as it was watery creamy with chicken fat on top. My son loved the grits/soup the first time but wouldn't eat this time. Order Kalbi on the side and was still pink inside. Banchans were all flavorless. But when mixed as bibimbap was edible and good. But better tasting it at LA's Gallerias Mall Market. Every banchan there is superior. If you dont know where the good banchan is then for non Koreans this would be a good introduction and place to experience home like cooking minus some flavor. For 2 adults and 1 child bill was $150. Would I go back? No. But if I had guest in town would take just for the experience of many dishes. If restaurant reading this review those deep fried  kimchi chuns are a waste of table space. Better off with regular kimchi, or vegetable chun. Yet for $35/ person can do shrimp or seafood pancakes. Inflation making it difficult for businesses, but cutting corners by diluting customers dont go back and get 0 business.

author: Faith
review_text: Authentic Korean cooking, everything was delish, especially the marinated spicy crab, a must!  Service was outstanding!

author: Coryne S Suzuki
review_text: First time here and I loved it! The staff was so kind and patient and explained their course menu. They took the time to nicely go over each of the dishes and how to eat them. Delicious and healthy, country-style Korean food. You can ask for more barley rice (we didn't but we observed several tables doing so).  Free parking in the parking lot on the back side of the restaurant.

author: S K
review_text:
For my first time here, I was incredibly impressed with the food lineup and flavors.
The meal started with pumpkin porridge and scorched-rice tea, and after just one taste of the porridge, I gave it a big thumbs-up!
I ordered the spicy marinated crab and boiled pork belly. The crab was perfectly prepared, and the seasoning was absolutely spot-on.
The quality is definitely comparable to a solid, traditional Korean restaurant. All the side dishes were also clean and well-made.
I felt the cheonggukjang (fermented soybean stew) was a little on the bland side, but it wasn't a deal-breaker at all, and it might just be my preference.
Overall, this was one of the most satisfying meals I've had in a long time. 👍👍👍👍👍👍👍

author: Vivi V
review_text: This was my first time trying food prepared this way, and it's very different from other Korean restaurants. On my initial visit, I found the staff friendly and the ambiance pleasant. The food was enjoyable, especially the combination of veggies with barley rice and sesame oil. The pancake and chicken perilla seed porridge  stood out as highlights. The set menu offers a substantial amount of food. Overall, it was a positive experience, and I would recommend this place.

author: Jane Lui
review_text: This is heaven for vegetarians/pescatarians. We got the set menu - 25 different dishes that all told and everything tasted so good. Not heavily spiced or salted, very clean eating. The roe, snail, and crab cakes were delicious!!! Incredibly sweet crew and explained what everything is. Fun atmosphere, have their own huge parking lot for the plaza which is so rare in ktown! A great birthday meal.

author: Jung Lee
review_text: This traditional Korean restaurant serves $30 set menu that includes a dozen plus side dishes and two soups with options to add sharing specialty dishes such as bosam (boiled pork belly) or LA grilled galbi. Most people are building their own bibimbap with these side dishes and adding the specialties dishes. So it feels different than eating at typical Korean restaurants. Entrance is in the rear parking lot. You walk in and add your name to the waitlist board. Most of the side dishes were good and the specialty dishes were ok. Suggest to order the minimum order of two set menus for a party of 4 and add some other dishes. There was a wait of 15 minutes when we went during weekend lunch.

author: Clara Lee
review_text:
Overall the meal was good but nothing special. As a korean it was kinda similar to the random assortment of stuff chucked into a bibimbap at a church lunch iykyk LOL
Th best part was probably the perilla chicken porridge. The marinted pork ribs are a NO for me they are not marinated long enough so only the exterior is coated in sauce and th inside is dry and flavorless.
Also the table got way full and 복잡해. Probably will not come again but glad i tried it at least once. Like. Its not bad. Its just nothing special. I appreciated the dessert though. Didnt appreciate the tone of the waitress with a lot of makeup, really pedantically switching to english to then explain the dishes very slowly even though im fluent in korean, and was in fact there with my parents and sister lol.

author: Daniel Acusar
review_text:
Great korean food. Menu was short and straightforward, but all the dishes on their set menu were flavorful and tasty.

This was an enjoyable dining experience where they just give you a whole bunch of options to put on your rice and all of them were good. Mix your own rice bowl with their plethora of vegetables.

I also liked the side salad but especially liked the Pork Ribs. Slightly spicy and very asian. Worth a try. Pricey but has large servings.

author: Kate Choi
review_text: The presentation of the dishes wasn’t bad, but it doesn’t taste like traditional Korean barley rice. The seasoning of each ingredient doesn’t harmonize well. I wouldn’t recommend this place because I’m worried people who haven’t tried real Korean barley rice might think this is what it’s supposed to taste like. If you’re craving bibimbap, I recommend the one at Jin Sol Gukbap, just one block away. I honestly don’t understand why this place has such good reviews. I wouldn’t go back again.

author: Sun Kim
review_text:
Have you ever wondered what the “real Korean food” looks and tastes like? THIS place is the place you have to visit!!! It is very traditional and very healthy place to go and eat. In fact, it’s so traditional that you’d be having hard time to find a place like this in Korea.

Food quality and taste is out of this world. Very healthy, refreshing, and rich. When you eat it, you don’t feel one of those “stuffed” feelings but feels like your body is being cleansed. Every bite makes you think you are not in the United States.

Entire staff, including the owner, are so nice and caring that you feel as if you are home.

I suggest you visit here during “awkward hours like 3pm or 4pm because I can guarantee you that this place will be PACKED during regular meal time. Due to that, I wish there are more staff available because there were only 3 servers that couldn’t handle all the volume.

WILL GO BACK FOR SURE

author: Krisell Canamaso
review_text:
I went on a Tuesday night and had a very easy time finding parking. There is free parking behind the restaurant and street parking. The entrance is also from the back of the restaurant.

Service was excellent. It felt like going to your friend's house and being helped by the kindest Korean mom. They don't have buttons at your table to request assistance but the staff is always walking around, incredibly attentive, and super warm and friendly. My entire group ordered the set and the food came out immediately. It being our first time, the server went over how to tackle the spread and explained the soups.

The food was excellent! So many delicious veggie banchan and the set is basically a BYOB - build your own bibimbap. There were lots of banchan I've never had before like chopped chili pepper, shishito pepper, eggplant, and a white mushroom that looked like a shorter seafood mushroom. My favorites were the small patty sized kimchi pancakes, the acorn jelly salad (could use more acorn jelly 😬), and the entire BYOB experience... that's pretty much all the food 😆 the sea snail dish was good but I wasn't a huge fan of the texture. I eat pescatarian and it reminded me of bony cartilage. The best part is that you can get unlimited Barley rice and banchan. It was so much food that we never finished our first set. We ended up taking the leftovers home and it was enough for another meal.

Overall, I would definitely go back and absolutely recommend it. There is an a la carte menu and I would love to try some of those dishes with a larger group.

author: Kelly Kang
review_text:
Of all the countless times I've visited Ktown this was my first time at Borit Gogae and was an absolutely wonderful experience. The restaurant offers an extensive banchan spread with barley rice, perfect for crafting your own bibimbap. Lots of plant based side dishes.

The set menu includes an appetizer of pumpkin porridge and nurungji, accompanied by tea and a delightful dessert. While the dukk galbi we tried was just okay, the overall set menu was impressive and something I would definitely return for. Note: you're required to order a minimum of two orders of the set menu.

Every dish tasted homemade and authentically Korean, a detail that I know my parents would particularly appreciate. We visited on a Monday afternoon for a late lunch and found plenty of free parking behind the restaurant.

Overall, Borit Gogae provides a cozy and authentic dining experience that I highly recommend.

author: johnnyprozac johnnyprozac
review_text: The reviewers who think this place is expensive are either delusional, out of touch or just stupid. This is an insane amount of quality flavorful food for the money. The reviewers who said the service was rude are probably themselves entitled, also delusional, and/or also stupid. The service was politely informative, efficient, and very quick. Note the reviewers who negatively rated this restaurant and you should actively believe the opposite of any place they review.

author: Yunah Hahn
review_text:
Excellent service, amazing food and healthy too!
The ambiance is very homey, nothing fancy yet that’s why we liked it. Good taste like grandma’s cooking. Very authentic, home made, healthy traditional style with no msg. Food is totally worth the price. If you’re getting the set meal, and if you love vegetable side dish, you’re in for a treat!
They also had some seafood side dish like the little clamb with soy based sauce, pickled spicy squid, conch salad with yuzu dressing. The chicken perilla seed soup and the chungookjang (fermented soy bean soup) was delicious as well. We enjoyed mixing all the veggies with barely rice and the bean paste sauce. Make sure you add some sesame oil though!
Galbi was also excellent though we were too busy eating all the banchans.

Overall, we thoroughly loved it and will definitely be back for more!

author: Mukund Kaushik
review_text:
If you want a rotisserie style chicken that is juicy and flavorful without being too spicy, and good value for money, Dino’s chicken does not disappoint.

The 1/2 chicken with fries tortillas and coleslaw is less than 20 bucks. It’s a no frills atmosphere with tables on the inside and some outside overlooking the street traffic. The parking is a bit tight but if you circle around enough times, you might get lucky.

Next time we will order the fries and the sauce on the side as they serve the chicken on top of the fries.

The place does not disappoint and this place is a “keeper” on my list.

author: Christopher Gorrie
review_text:
I didn’t know what to expect when coming here, but I’m sure glad that I did! I ordered a half chicken with rice and beans, which also came with complimentary coleslaw and corn tortillas.
